brief: ZeroHedge relays two AI-credit reads. JPMorgan's Cembalest: 2026 debt issuance by the five hyperscalers plus NVIDIA is about $320bn, of which an estimated $303bn is ten-year equivalents, 68% of new Treasury long duration borrowing this year, so hyperscaler supply may be creating a supply-demand problem at the long end. Goldman FICC IG specialist Jeffrey Papai: the AI versus non-AI supply technical flips in September. AI supply of about $300bn year to date slows to one more senior hyperscaler deal plus some datacenters, the lowest of any period since the buildout began by almost 50%, which sets up a temporary relief rally in AI spreads (GSUCIABK) he would own for one to two months and then sell, because rough non-official estimates put 2027 senior hyperscaler/chip issuance about 40% higher at $340bn while only $45bn matures, so demand is not replenished. On the non-AI side, about $230bn of September supply leaves generic IG vulnerable, but yield-based demand is robust, so he would buy the kneejerk dip (GSIG30NH). Risk transfer is expanding across products: CDS volumes on pace up about 15%, TRS growing, IG and HY cash volumes up 10-15% year over year.
